# ADR-0006: API clients are generated by NSwag and never edited by hand

- **Date:** Author to confirm. First evidence in git: the generator script exists from `bdc6ab4` (2026-05-24); regenerations appear throughout the history (`git log --grep="NSwag"`).
- **Status:** Proposed (draft reconstructed from the repository, not yet confirmed by the author)

## Context

- The backend exposes three OpenAPI documents, one per controller group (`cinema`, `identity`, `payment`). `cinemabe/Cinema/1-Service/Cinema.Service.Clients/Generator/GenerateNswag.ps1` and the three `*.nswag` files generate both the C# clients (`Cinema.Service.Clients/**`) and the Angular services (`cinemafe/projects/CinemaLib/src/lib/services/*-http.service.ts`).
- `AGENTS.md`: never hand-edit generated files; regenerate with the script, run from its own `Generator/` directory with the Web API host stopped, or it fails with path or lock errors.
- Every contract change is followed by a regeneration commit, for example `30d81f5` (per-theater loyalty), `c546da0` (review/search endpoints), `ad67d30` (after Cancel Booking removal).

## Decision

The frontend and any .NET client call the API only through generated clients. A change to a controller, DTO or enum is carried to the clients by regeneration, in a separate `chore(...): regenerate NSwag clients` commit.

Author to confirm: why generation was chosen over hand-written HTTP services (for example keeping the Angular and C# contracts in step with the controllers).

## Consequences

- Frontend types and enum values come from the backend, so a renamed DTO field fails the Angular build at compile time instead of at run time.
- Generated files make large diffs and must be regenerated whenever an endpoint or DTO changes; a stale client would call an old contract. Nothing in CI regenerates and compares them. Author to confirm whether it should.
- Enum-to-label lookups for the generated enums are centralized in `CinemaLib`'s `cinema.model.ts` (`AGENTS.md`).
- Regeneration needs the host stopped and a specific working directory, which is an extra manual step.

## Alternatives considered

- **Hand-written HTTP services and DTO types in each app.** Not shown in the repository. Author to confirm: why generation was chosen over them.
- **One document and client for the whole API.** The repository used a separate `staff` document until `14246b5` removed it, and keeps `cinema`, `identity` and `payment` as separate documents. Author to confirm: why three documents rather than one.
